S001@7611-7692.words: do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work
S001@7611-7692.reason: The judgement says nearly all studies had low confidence in their findings, which bears on how far the evidence shows that these education programmes work.

S001@7900-8058.reason: The judgement describes the education gap and its cause (school systems not set up for different impairments) without evaluating any programme, which the scope excludes as descriptive data on the gap.

S001@8059-8153.reason: The judgement concerns interventions to equalise health outcomes, which the scope explicitly excludes as non-education outcomes, so it does not bear on whether programmes improve education.

S001@8154-8406.reason: The judgement recommends a twin-track approach, combining disability-specific support with inclusion in mainstream activities such as teacher skills and classroom accessibility, which bears directly on which kinds of programme work best for children with disabilities.

S001@8407-8703.reason: The judgement describes what kinds of interventions the systematic review evaluated (mostly child-level rather than school- or system-level), which bears on weighing evidence about which programme types work best.

S001@8704-8859.reason: The judgement says evaluation should focus on interventions that target both the individual with a disability and their wider environment, which bears on which kinds of programme work best and on what the evidence covers.
